bull.t: Dakota Lithium acquisition expands specialty-market reach
bull.b: The Dakota Lithium acquisition broadens Dragonfly’s product portfolio and distribution across specialty battery markets. Its existing revenue base and use of Dragonfly’s commercial infrastructure could add scale, while management expects the business to become adjusted-EBITDA accretive in Q4.

bull.t: Heavy-duty trucking provides a new growth channel
bull.b: The trucking business creates a developing channel beyond Dragonfly’s softer RV market. Revenue growth from fleet pilots and broader deployments could diversify demand, increase commercial battery volumes, and improve operating leverage if customer conversions continue through year-end.

Additional patent allowances reinforce Dragonfly’s proprietary position in dry-electrode and solid-state battery technology. Broader geographic protection can support future commercialization and partnerships, while creating intellectual-property differentiation in advanced energy storage markets.

bear.t: Persistent losses and cash burn weaken financial sustainability
bear.b: Large ongoing losses and deeply negative operating and free cash flow show that the business is not yet self-funding. Continued cash burn can constrain investment in growth, increase dependence on financing, and leave less flexibility if operational improvements take longer than planned.

bear.t: RV weakness and declining revenue pressure scale
bear.b: Dragonfly remains exposed to weakness in its important RV end market, which is pressuring direct-to-consumer and some OEM demand. Declining revenue makes it harder to absorb fixed costs and reach the approximately $70M annualized sales run rate needed for targeted profitability.

bear.t: Nasdaq equity non-compliance creates financing and listing risk
bear.b: The Nasdaq deficiency highlights pressure on Dragonfly’s capital structure and introduces uncertainty around continued listing. A prolonged compliance problem could reduce access to public equity markets and impair liquidity, financing flexibility, and stakeholder confidence over the coming quarters.
